analysis.note: Whole compound stem inflected as a masculine nominative singular adjective to the implied anyaḥ samādhi/nirodha. Internally, virāma-pratyaya is understood from the bhāṣya as an objectless/contentless cessation-cognition, and abhyāsa as its practice.

verification.detail: compound stem virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrva as Pum/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Qualifies the implied samādhi/nirodha: not a standalone subject ‘the residue of saṃskāras,’ but a state in which saṃskāra remains after the vṛttis have ceased.

verification.detail: compound stem saṃskāraśeṣa as Pum/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Refers to the other samādhi, identified by Vyāsa as asaṃprajñāta/nirbīja samādhi, i.e. the mind’s nirodha.

justifications.decision: Resolve the implied subject and referent of anyaḥ.
options_considered: the other samādhi, asaṃprajñāta/nirbīja, as distinct from the preceding samprajñāta
justifications.chosen: anyaḥ means the other samādhi, namely asaṃprajñāta/nirbīja samādhi, described as nirodha of the mind.

evidence.quote: sarvavṛttipratyastamaye saṃskāraśeṣo nirodhaś cittasya samādhir asaṃprajñātaḥ.
evidence.translation: When all mental activities have set, the mind’s nirodha, with saṃskāra as remainder, is asaṃprajñāta samādhi.

evidence.quote: tadabhyāsapūrvakaṃ hi cittaṃ nirālambanam abhāvaprāptam iva bhavatīty eṣa nirbījaḥ samādhir asaṃprajñātaḥ.
evidence.translation: For the mind, preceded by practice of that, becomes supportless, as though it had reached absence; this is seedless samādhi, asaṃprajñāta.

options_considered: pratyaya as ordinary belief or conviction
pratyaya as a real object-cognition of cessation
justifications.chosen: virāma-pratyaya is the objectless/contentless cessation-cognition taken as an ālambana, not an ordinary object-supported idea or merely a ‘belief’.

evidence.quote: sālambano hy abhyāsas tatsādhanāya na kalpata iti virāmapratyayo nirvastuka ālambanīkriyate.
evidence.translation: For object-supported practice is not fit as a means to it; therefore the virāma-pratyaya, objectless, is made the support.
And it is empty of an object/content.

evidence.quote: sarvavṛttipratyastamaye saṃskāraśeṣo nirodhaś cittasya samādhir asaṃprajñātaḥ.
evidence.translation: At the setting of all vṛttis, the nirodha of the mind with saṃskāra as remainder is asaṃprajñāta samādhi.

justifications.decision: Construe the compound relation of abhyāsa-pūrva in virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrvaḥ.
options_considered: something prior to the practice of virāma-pratyaya
the samādhi/nirodha preceded or conditioned by practice of the virāma-pratyaya
justifications.chosen: virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrvaḥ means ‘preceded by, or having as its prior condition, the practice of the virāma-pratyaya’.

evidence.quote: tadabhyāsapūrvakaṃ hi cittaṃ nirālambanam abhāvaprāptam iva bhavatīty eṣa nirbījaḥ samādhir asaṃprajñātaḥ.
evidence.translation: For the mind, having the practice of that as its prior condition, becomes supportless, as though it had reached absence; this is seedless samādhi, asaṃprajñāta.

evidence.quote: sālambano hy abhyāsas tatsādhanāya na kalpata iti virāmapratyayo nirvastuka ālambanīkriyate.
evidence.translation: Object-supported practice is not fit as a means to it; therefore the objectless virāma-pratyaya is taken as the support.

options_considered: ‘a remaining saṃskāra’ as the main subject
‘the residue of saṃskāras’ as a substantive
a samādhi/nirodha-state in which only saṃskāra remains after cessation of vṛttis
justifications.chosen: saṃskāraśeṣaḥ is bahuvrīhi in force: the samādhi/nirodha has saṃskāra as the remaining residue after all vṛttis cease; it is not total annihilation.

evidence.quote: sarvavṛttipratyastamaye saṃskāraśeṣo nirodhaś cittasya samādhir asaṃprajñātaḥ.
evidence.translation: When all vṛttis have set, the mind’s nirodha, with saṃskāra as remainder, is asaṃprajñāta samādhi.

evidence.quote: tadabhyāsapūrvakaṃ hi cittaṃ nirālambanam abhāvaprāptam iva bhavatīty eṣa nirbījaḥ samādhir asaṃprajñātaḥ.
evidence.translation: The mind, preceded by the practice of that, becomes supportless, as though it had reached absence; this is seedless samādhi, asaṃprajñāta.

translation: The other [samādhi], preceded by the practice (abhyāsa) of the cessation-cognition (virāma-pratyaya), has only latent impressions (saṃskāra) remaining.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might leave anyaḥ vague; Vyāsa identifies it as asaṃprajñāta, nirbīja samādhi, the mind’s nirodha.
It might render pratyaya as ordinary ‘belief’ or ‘conviction’; Vyāsa makes the virāma-pratyaya an objectless, contentless ālambana.
It might take saṃskāraśeṣaḥ as a substantive ‘remainder of impressions’; the bhāṣya construes it adjectivally with samādhi/nirodha: the vṛttis have ceased, but saṃskāra remains.
It might read the state as simple non-being; Vyāsa says the mind becomes as though it had reached absence, while still being saṃskāra-śeṣa.
